verdict_label: Common between men, not across genders
explanation: Among friends of the same gender, greetings in Saudi Arabia often include cheek-kissing — typically the left hand rests on the other person's right shoulder while leaning in for three kisses, either right-left-right or repeated on the same cheek. Between men and women who are not closely related, physical greetings are avoided altogether; it's best to greet verbally and wait to see if a hand is extended.
local_tip: With someone of the same gender who initiates a cheek-kiss greeting, follow their lead; with the opposite gender, default to a verbal greeting unless they extend a hand first.

also_check.note: Same-gender cheek-kissing and warm embraces are common, while cross-gender greetings stay more reserved.
Cheek-kissing between close friends of the same gender is common, though cross-gender greetings in public are more conservative.
Cheek-kissing isn't a traditional greeting; a bow or handshake is expected instead.

sources.title: A Handshake is Worth 1000 Words: Body Language in Dubai Business Culture
